proposal.thesis: DexCom reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.308B (+13% YoY reported, +12% organic, per the 2026-07-30 earnings release), beat EPS estimates by 15.1% (fourth straight beat), and raised full-year revenue guidance to $5.18-5.25B while lifting non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 23.5-24% -- GAAP operating margin already expanded 590bps YoY to 24.3% this quarter. Note: the bundle's digest field states 26.3% YoY revenue growth for DXCM, which conflicts with the source earnings release's own stated 13%/12% organic figure -- I am citing the sourced, lower number as the reliable one and flagging the discrepancy rather than using the more flattering figure. The balance sheet is net cash (-0.81x net debt/EBITDA, $1.95B cash, minimal debt), TTM free cash flow more than doubled to $1.405B, and the company is returning capital (3.88% TTM buyback yield, diluted shares down 4.4% YoY). Ownership_flow shows institutional accumulation aligned with the rising price, and sell-side has been raising targets all week (BTIG to $90, Stifel to $95, Truist to $93, WebSearch-verified, not bundle-sourced) following the print. The stock pulled back 4.92% in its most recent session after tagging a 52-week high three sessions earlier -- I could not confirm a specific negative catalyst for that single-session drop through today's degraded news feed, so I am treating it as digestion after a strong run (RSI 61.5, not overbought; still above both the 50- and 200-day averages) rather than a broken thesis, and sizing/stopping so that I am proven wrong cheaply if it is more than that.
catalysts: Q2 FY2026 earnings beat + raised FY26 revenue guidance to $5.18-5.25B (~11-13% growth), reported 2026-07-30
Sell-side price target increases this week: BTIG to $90, Stifel to $95, Truist to $93 (WebSearch-verified, not in bundle)
Stelo OTC CGM relaunch (new AI-driven insights app, expanded Type 2 non-insulin access) widening the addressable market beyond core insulin users
proposal.macro_context: SPY is above both its 50-DMA ($745.72) and 200-DMA ($699.04), up 3.0% over the past month, and the regime hint scores 4/5 'supportive.' Momentum health is 'healthy' (no factor unwind) and breadth within my tracked universe is broad (100% of names above their 200-DMA, 88.9% beating SPY over 1 month, n=9, small sample). One geopolitical flag is active (Ukraine drone strike on a Russian refinery) but it hasn't moved oil materially and doesn't bear on DXCM. DXCM itself sits outside my AI-stack theme entirely (ai_neutral, demand_driver=healthcare) with low correlation to my only holding (0.09 corr_to_book, beta 0.59 vs BKR's 0.54) -- a genuine diversifier rather than another AI-adjacent bet, which fits a supportive-but-selective tape where I would rather not stack a single factor.
proposal.risk_map: This fails if: (1) the Aug-5 ~5% one-day drop turns out to reflect a real negative catalyst I could not identify through today's degraded news feeds -- early tell is a further close below $78 on rising volume; (2) inventory-to-revenue is deteriorating (55.5% vs 49.3% a year ago per quality_ratios) -- if that shows up as a Q3 sell-through miss rather than a capacity-ramp build, the growth story cracks; (3) options positioning already shows a mild put lean (P/C vol 1.17, +3.3pp put skew, low confidence given free-chain data) -- a modest signal some money is hedging further downside; (4) medtech/growth multiples are duration-sensitive and the 10-year yield is rising (4.63%, up from 4.36% three months ago) -- a continued back-up in rates would compress growth multiples broadly, DXCM included, independent of company execution.
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: Wall Street is already bullish -- strong_buy consensus across 25 analysts (recommendation_mean 1.32), mean target $93.44 (13% above the $82.66 close), with BTIG, Stifel and Truist all raising targets to $90-95 this week after the 2026-07-30 Q2 beat-and-raise. MY VIEW: consensus targets still lag what a genuine growth-and-margin reacceleration deserves -- the Street's models were anchored to the 'slowing 2026 growth' caution management gave earlier this year, and have not fully re-rated for two consecutive quarters of upside plus a 590bp operating-margin expansion (18.37% to 24.33% YoY) and an expanding Stelo/Type-2 TAM. MECHANISM: sell-side revenue models likely still discount the raised $5.18-5.25B FY26 guide as conservative-beat bait rather than a genuine inflection, so the multiple (31.2x forward earnings on 20%+ growth with margins improving) has not re-rated to reflect the new growth-plus-margin combination the way it would for a comparably-positioned med-tech compounder. RESOLUTION: the next print (~2026-10-29) either confirms the reacceleration continues -- in which case the multiple re-rates toward the higher end of the new analyst targets -- or it does not, which is exactly what my stop and time-box are there to catch.

thesis_invalidators.invalidating_print: Q3 FY2026 results (~2026-10-29) showing reported revenue growth below the ~11% low end of the just-raised $5.18-5.25B FY26 guide, or non-GAAP operating margin missing the guided 23.5-24% range.
thesis_invalidators.invalidating_structure: A daily close below $78.00 on above-average volume, breaking the noise-band stop and confirming the pullback is not just digestion.
thesis_invalidators.time_box: If DXCM has not reclaimed and held above $87 (near its 52-week high) within 25 trading days of entry (by ~2026-09-11), the post-earnings-drift thesis isn't playing out -- reassess.
